title: Choose the visual world for the beauty theme
question: The roll assigned The Attar Stall. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Attar Stall
options.lineage: Gulf souk attar & beauty stalls — tiered shelves, ranks of small bottles, hand-lettered price cards, brass trays
options.thesis: Abundance you can read: products stand in dense, ordered tiers on shelf lines, every one with its own price card — the opposite of the airy pastel beauty page.
options.viewport: Header as the stall's awning strip (announcement + nav); hero is not a carousel but a tiered shelf of the merchant's slider images and featured products; below, each product group is one shelf tier you scroll along, every card a small bottle-like tile with a price card hanging under it.
options.risk: Density must stay ordered — one tier too many and the shelf becomes clutter; merchant photos must sit inside consistent tiles so the shelf stays calm.

raised.raise: State is a mark, not a hue: sold-out is a folded price card, sale is a second card clipped over the first, selected filters are pinned tags — never colour washes.
Every tile carries the same facts band in the same place: price · stock · SKU — the trusted counter's honesty as a fixed label, not a tooltip.
Integer shelf grid: tiers snap to a fixed pitch at every breakpoint; narrow screens drop tiles per tier, never tile size.
Objects are the navigation: the shelf, the tray, the tag — you browse by handling them, no abstract chrome.

options.label: The Counter Card
options.lineage: department-store beauty counter tester trays and shade cards
options.thesis: Every product presented the way the counter assistant hands it to you: on a white tester tray, shade dots first, facts printed on the card.
options.viewport: A tray grid of products with shade chips leading, a sticky facts card on the product page.
options.risk: This is the direction most runs land on for beauty — familiar by design; it wins on clarity, not on memory.

options.label: Industrial Quote Grammar
options.lineage: industrial streetwear — straight-quoted labels, zip-tie tags, hazard diagonals
options.thesis: Every zone named literally in straight quotes, the active thing keeps its orange tag on.
options.viewport: A stockroom grid of garments, each plate labelled "JACKET" in quotes, the cart tag swinging orange.
options.case: Fuses for the fashion half of the boutique and for fact-first labelling; loses clarity for cosmetics (shades, ingredients read as slogans).
options.risk: Reads as a streetwear drop, not a trusted counter.

options.label: Magazine Shingle
options.lineage: Japanese street-fashion magazine spreads — cut-out figures, handwritten price call-outs
options.thesis: The boutique as a crowded spread: products shingled, every one with a hand-priced call-out on a leader line.
options.viewport: Overlapping product cut-outs across the first screen, prices on leader lines, one figure lifting on hover.
options.case: Holds the young boutique audience and prices-front clarity; loses the trusted-counter calm and breaks on merchant photos that are not cut-outs.
options.risk: Chaos unless the merchant ships cut-out imagery, which most do not.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.thesis: Products as frames on a perforated rail.
options.viewport: A horizontal strip of frames crossing the page.
options.case: Fuses poorly: beauty shoppers do not identify with an editing bench; frame pitch fights product imagery.
options.kept: State is a mark, not a hue — donated to the shelf.

options.label: Leather Studio
options.thesis: Digital things rendered as loved objects on wood.
options.viewport: A wooden shelf with leather headers.
options.case: Fuses poorly: dated rendering and the wrong material for cosmetics; wins nothing on clarity.

options.label: Brine Calendar
options.thesis: Jars ranked on shelf lines, each label banded with facts.
options.viewport: A shelf of jars with date bands.
options.case: Fuses poorly: fermentation has no audience overlap; the fixed facts band is the one discipline worth keeping.
options.kept: Fixed facts band per tile — donated.

options.label: One-bit Desktop
options.thesis: Every tone as dither, windows as navigation.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no colour means no shades, no merchant palette; audience mismatch.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The beauty storefront everyone ships: blush neutrals, thin serif display, airy product grid, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Full-bleed lifestyle hero, serif headline, four-up product grid.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other beauty shop by design.
